newsitem.title: USA: LL&E Bighorn well flowing at 44 MMCFD.
newsitem.headline: LL&E Bighorn well flowing at 44 MMCFD.

text.p: The Louisiana Land and Exploration Co said Wednesday that a well it was operating in the Madden Field in Fremont County, Wyoming was flowing 44 million cubic feet of gas per day (MMCFD) through a one-inch choke with 4,964 PSI flowing tubing pressure.
The company said in a statement the surface shut-in pressure prior to testing was measured at 6,700 pounds per square inch (PSI) at the step-out well, known as Bighorn 4-36.
The company said it drilled the well, the third one in the deep Madison Formation, to a total depth of 24,600 feet to a location 1,000 feet downdip from the crest of the structure.
"(It) has proved a productive area of at least 23 square miles," it said.

"The test rate of the well was constrained by the capacity of the production test equipment at the location," it said. "A four-point production test indicated a calculated absolute open flow potential of 240 MMCFD."
The well encountered 198 feet of pay with no water level present and excellent reservoir quality, it added.
The first two Madison wells, Bighorn 1-5 and 2-3, are together producing about 52 MMCFD, the company said.
As operator, Louisiana Land owns a 38-percent working interest in the well.
Other working interest owners include W.A. Moncrief with 36 percent, North Central Oil Corp with 14 percent, and BHP Petroleum (Americas) Inc with 12 percent.
